text.p: The population of the Falkland Islands, the south Atlantic archipelago that triggered a war between Britain and Argentina in 1982, has risen to an all-time high, official figures showed on Friday.
Not including the British garrison, the population stands at 2,564 compared with 2,392 in 1931, the previous high, according to an official census conducted in April 1996.

The farming population on the islands has fallen to 445 from 653 in 1986 while the population in the capital Port Stanley has risen to 1,638 from about 1,000 before the Falklands War which maintained British sovereignity over the islands.
The imbalance between men and women on the islands, about two to one in the 1980s, has been redressed and the populations are approaching parity.

Before the war, many local girls would marry British soldiers and move to Britain. But such marriages are now rare because the British troops live on an isolated base and have an average tour of duty of four months rather than a year.
The 856 households on the windswept islands run 1,364 registered vehicles and own 779 televisions between them. The size of the British garrison is not divulged.
